definitions.explanation: To look at and comprehend written text. Used for books, newspapers, signs, emails, and any written material.
To speak written words out loud, as in reading poetry or reading to someone.
To anticipate or predict something, as in 'reading' a situation or someone's intentions. {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む means to read the atmosphere/room.

examples.japanese: {新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}んでいる。
この{漢字|かんじ}は{読|よ}めますか。
{小|ちい}さい{字|じ}は{読|よ}みにくい。
examples.english: Small letters are hard to read.

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのが{好|す}きで、{毎晩|まいばん}{少|すこ}しずつ{読|よ}んでいる。
examples.english: I like reading books before bed and read a little every night.

examples.japanese: {声|こえ}に{出|だ}して{読|よ}んで。
{子供|こども}に{絵本|えほん}を{読|よ}んであげた。
examples.english: I read a picture book to the child.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{教科書|きょうかしょ}を{読|よ}んでくれた。
examples.english: The teacher read the textbook aloud for us.

examples.japanese: {毎晩|まいばん}{子供|こども}に{本|ほん}を{読|よ}み{聞|き}かせるのが{私|わたし}の{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: Reading books aloud to my child every night is something I enjoy.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}の{心|こころ}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: I read the other person's feelings.

examples.japanese: {先|さき}を{読|よ}んで{行動|こうどう}する。
examples.english: I act after predicting what will happen.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{次|つぎ}の{手|て}を{読|よ}むことができた。
examples.english: I was able to predict his next move.

examples.japanese: {空気|くうき}が{読|よ}めない{人|ひと}は、{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}を{困|こま}らせることがある。
examples.english: People who can't read the room sometimes trouble those around them.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb. Pattern: Xを{読|よ}む (read X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action. {読|よ}んでいる = 'is reading.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む (read a book)
・{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}む (read newspaper)
・{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む (read the room - idiom)
・{声|こえ}に{出|だ}して{読|よ}む (read aloud)

Godan verb: te-form {読|よ}んで. Cultural: {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む refers to understanding social cues. KY = {空気|くうき}{読|よ}めない (can't read the room).
